title: Greatest common divisor
prompt:
Write gcd(a, b) that returns the greatest common divisor of two positive whole numbers: the biggest number that divides both exactly.
Example: gcd(12, 18) = 6.
hints: List the divisors of 12 and of 18 by hand. Which are shared, and which is largest?
There's an old trick by Euclid: the gcd of a and b is the same as the gcd of b and the remainder of a divided by b. When can you stop?
Plan: while b is not 0, replace (a, b) with (b, a % b); when b reaches 0, a is the answer.

edge_hints.same: gcd(n, n) is n. Check your loop still ends with the right variable.
edge_hints.one: 1 divides everything, so the answer must be 1.
